title: Algebra machines
goal: I can find the rule of a number machine from a table and write it with a letter. I can run a machine backwards to solve an equation.

learn.intro: A number machine follows a rule: IN goes in and OUT comes out. We write the rule with a letter, such as OUT = 4n + 3. To find the IN for a given OUT, run the machine backwards and undo the last step first.

example.problem: A machine does × 7, then − 4. OUT is 45. What was IN?
steps: Undo the last step first. Undo take away 4 by adding 4: 45 + 4 = 49.

howto.title: How to run a machine backwards
steps: Write the steps in order, from IN to OUT.
Start at OUT. Undo the last step first.
Use the opposite step: + undoes −, and × undoes ÷.
Check by running the machine forwards.

try.text: A machine does × 4, then + 9. OUT is 41. What was IN? {b}
try.explanation: Undo the last step first: 41 − 9 = 32. Then undo × 4: 32 ÷ 4 = 8. Check: 8 × 4 + 9 = 41.

items.text: Guess my rule. The rule is: multiply n by a number, then add a number.
items.explanation: IN goes up 2 and OUT goes up 6, so each 1 of IN adds 3: × 3. 3 × 1 = 3 but OUT is 5, so add 2: OUT = 3n + 2. IN 10 gives 32. For OUT 50: 3n = 48, n = 16.

items.text: Guess my rule. This time the machine takes a number away.
items.explanation: IN goes up 2 and OUT goes up 6, so × 3. 3 × 2 = 6 but OUT is 1, so take away 5: OUT = 3n − 5. IN 20 gives 55. For OUT 100: 3n = 105, n = 35.

items.text: A machine does 2 steps. Look at the first IN and OUT.
items.explanation: IN 5 times 3 is 15, so the middle box is 15. 15 + 4 = 19, so the last step is add 4. IN 9: 9 × 3 = 27, then 27 + 4 = 31.

items.text: Machine P does × 2, then + 6. Machine Q does + 6, then × 2. Use the same IN for both.

parts.label: a
parts.text: IN 7:  P gives {b}  and Q gives {b}.

parts.label: b
parts.text: IN 10:  P gives {b}  and Q gives {b}.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Do P and Q give the same OUT?   {circ:Yes|No}

items.explanation: IN 7: P gives 7 × 2 = 14, then 20. Q gives 7 + 6 = 13, then 26. IN 10: P gives 26 and Q gives 32. The order of the steps matters, so P and Q do not give the same OUT.

items.text: The block "answer" holds the number you type. In code, × means times. Predict what the sprite says.
items.explanation: out = answer × 4 − 3. Type 9: 36 − 3 = 33. Type 25: 100 − 3 = 97. For 61, run it backwards: 61 + 3 = 64, then 64 ÷ 4 = 16.

items.text: Plan a search. Find n when 7n − 4 = 73 by trying n = 0, 1, 2, ... Fill in the blanks.
items.explanation: The search starts at 0 and adds 1 each time, until 7 × n − 4 is 73. 7 × 10 − 4 = 66 is too small and 7 × 11 − 4 = 73. It says 11. Check backwards: 73 + 4 = 77 and 77 ÷ 7 = 11.

items.text: Siti has n marbles. Kumar has 5 marbles more. Jenny has 3 times as many marbles as Siti.

parts.label: a
parts.text: When n = 8, Kumar has {b} and Jenny has {b}.

parts.label: b
parts.text: When n = 8, all 3 together have {b} stickers.

items.explanation: Kumar has n + 5 and Jenny has 3 × n. When n = 8: Kumar has 13, Jenny has 24, and all 3 together have 8 + 13 + 24 = 45. In general n + (n + 5) + 3n = 5n + 5.

items.text: Run each machine backwards to find n. Check by going forwards.
A phone plan costs 12 dollars a month, plus 3 dollars for each extra GB. n is the number of extra GB.

parts.label: c
parts.text: With 60 dollars you can buy {b} extra GB.

items.explanation: Cost = 3 × n + 12. 5 extra GB cost 3 × 5 + 12 = 27 dollars. For 60 dollars: 3n + 12 = 60, so 3n = 48 and n = 16.

items.text: Pick a number. Add 4. Multiply by 3. Subtract 9. Divide by 3. Subtract the number you picked.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Start with n. The steps give n + 4, 3n + 12, 3n + 3, n + 1, then {b}.

items.explanation: Start with 7: 11, 33, 24, 8, then 8 − 7 = 1. Start with 12: 16, 48, 39, 13, then 1. With n: n + 4, 3n + 12, 3n + 3, n + 1, then n + 1 − n = 1. Always 1.

items.text: Predict what the sprite says.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Two different numbers make it say 8. They are {b} and {b}.

items.explanation: 6 is not more than 10, so it says 12. 15 is more than 10, so it says 5. Says 8: answer − 10 = 8 gives 18, answer × 2 = 8 gives 4.

items.text: Machine X does × 2, then + 3. Its OUT goes straight into Machine Y, which does × 3, then − 4.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Joined, the rule is OUT = {b} × n + {b}.

items.hint: For OUT 77, undo Y first, then undo X.
items.explanation: IN 5: X gives 13, Y gives 39 − 4 = 35. For OUT 77, undo Y: (77 + 4) ÷ 3 = 27, then undo X: (27 − 3) ÷ 2 = 12. Joined rule: 3(2n + 3) − 4 = 6n + 5. Check: 6 × 12 + 5 = 77.

items.text: Ali is n years old. His brother is 4 years older. Their mother is 3 times as old as Ali. Together the 3 of them are 64 years old.
items.hint: Add up the n boxes first. Then add the extra 4.
items.explanation: Ali n, brother n + 4, mother 3n. Together: n + (n + 4) + 3n = 5n + 4 = 64. So 5n = 60 and n = 12. Ali is 12, his brother is 16 and their mother is 36. Check: 12 + 16 + 36 = 64.

items.text: A machine multiplies IN by a whole number, then adds or subtracts a whole number. IN 3 gives OUT 13 and IN 8 gives OUT 38.

parts.label: a
parts.text: When IN goes up by 5, OUT goes up by {b}.

items.hint: How much does OUT go up for each 1 that IN goes up?
items.explanation: IN goes up 5 (3 to 8) and OUT goes up 25 (13 to 38), so the × part is 25 ÷ 5 = 5. 5 × 3 = 15, but OUT is 13, so take away 2: OUT = 5n − 2. For OUT 98: 5n = 100 and n = 20.

Beyond Level 6: n on both sides.
Machine A does × 4, then + 1. Machine B does × 2, then + 13.

parts.label: a
parts.text: IN 2: A gives {b} and B gives {b}.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A and B give the same OUT when IN is {b}. That OUT is {b}.

items.hint: Make a table of IN, A and B. Look at how the gap changes.
items.explanation: IN 2: A gives 9 and B gives 17, so B is ahead by 8. A gains 2 for every 1 of IN, so the lead is gone in 4 steps, at IN 6. Both give 25. As an equation, 4n + 1 = 2n + 13 gives 2n = 12.

items.text: A search program tries n = 0, 1, 2, ... It stops when 7n − 3 is greater than 120.
items.hint: Is 7n − 3 greater than 120? Careful with equal.
items.explanation: 7n − 3 > 120 needs 7n > 123, so n > 17.57: n = 18 gives 123. It says 18, and OUT is 123. If 120 changes to 123, then 123 is not greater than 123, so it keeps going to n = 19.

items.text: IN 1, 2, 3, 4 give OUT 6, 11, 16, 21. The rule is OUT = {b} × n + {b}.
items.explanation: OUT goes up 5 for each 1 of IN, so × 5. 5 × 1 = 5, and OUT is 6, so add 1: OUT = 5n + 1.
